summary: Interpreted the control receipt and closed the child question's last stated gap. Receipt 531b0a48500843228e26623ce7333943 ran the same cluster scenario twice in one execution with the restart's Config.RestoreCommittedLogs setting as the only difference, and all seven mode-conditioned comparisons matched their declarations: the feature-on run's restart reported the stale {A,B,C} (violated, index 1), its two-voter partition elected a leader (violated, index 2) and its restarted node applied a write of its own (violated, index 3), while the feature-off run over the identical fixture reported {A,B,C,D,E} (holds, index 6), elected no leader in that partition (holds, index 7), had exactly one leader (holds, index 7) and applied nothing on the restarted node (holds, index 8). The experiment-level interpretation is explained/asserted with those indices and the mechanism traced to the replay skipping the committed configuration entry versus the control's scan covering it; the child question's account now treats the no-feature restart control as evidence instead of an open limitation, and the parent account was revised the same way, with joint histories rewritten for the six-receipt chain and the scan behaviour knowledge gaining the control restart event as a direct use. I also recorded that cluster-wide applied-write consistency is not a meaningful predicate in the control run, which is why its comparisons use the restarted node's own applied writes. Incomplete: a long-run window over the divergent state, the user Restore and term-changing truncation repair paths, and the operational frequency of the fall-behind that triggers the snapshot repair.
